requirement:
Usage MUST record mandatory input counts and sizes by evidence kind, in UTF-8
bytes and lines, and the same information for additional inputs requested through
`habeas` or `ripgrep`. A requirements input MUST also record its number of matched declarations.
Usage MUST distinguish unique inputs from repeated reads, successful from
failed reads, and prepared inputs from those actually sent to the model.
File-discovery calls MUST count as tool calls without recording directory
listings as evidence or source inputs.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** Each obligation maps to marked `{impl}` code and to at least one `{test}`. I found no unmarked code that implements part of it. I read it as met even though a few choices are open to interpretation (listed at the end).

**Obligations and implementation**

- **Sizes and kinds for mandatory and additional inputs.**
  - `UsageLog::prepared` (src/authoring/usage.rs:132) pushes one `InputUsage` per input.
  - Each entry records `origin`, `kind`, `bytes` and `lines`. `origin` is "mandatory" or the tool name (habeas, ripgrep). `kind` is outline, requirements or definition.
  - `bytes` is the UTF-8 byte length of the text lines plus the joining newlines. `lines` is the number of text lines.
  - `configured_record` (src/authoring/mod.rs:337) calls it for the mandatory inputs. `assess` calls it with the tool name for each tool delivery. The tool name covers habeas, ripgrep and any other delivery.
- **Matched declarations for a requirements input.** `components` is the length of the `matches` array, and 1 when there is none. The unit test checks 2 for a two-match requirements input.
- **Unique versus repeated reads.** `unique` is set from `self.seen.insert(input.to_string())`, so an identical repeated delivery is marked `unique: false`.
- **Successful versus failed reads.** `UsageLog::tool` (src/authoring/usage.rs:222) counts per-tool calls and, when the call failed, per-tool `tool_failures`. `assess` calls it with the failure flag for both success and error results. `skipped_tool` records calls skipped because of a submission.
- **Prepared versus sent to the model.**
  - `prepared` leaves `submitted_in_request` and `sent_in_request` as `None`.
  - `begin_request` sets `submitted_in_request` for every input not yet submitted.
  - `end_request` sets `sent_in_request` only when the response carried usage. A failed attempt therefore leaves it unset, and a later retry fills it in.
- **File discovery counts as a tool call without being an input.**
  - `list_files` (src/authoring/tools.rs:168) returns `inputs: Vec::new()`, so no directory listing is recorded as input or evidence.
  - `assess` still calls `usage.tool(name, …)` for every call, so the listing counts as a tool call.

**Tests**

- `input_metadata_counts_components_and_reads_without_persisting_source` (usage.rs:363) covers these points:
  - kind, bytes (including the multibyte `λ`), lines, components and `unique`;
  - origin;
  - the null-to-submitted-to-sent progression;
  - that no source content is persisted.
- `failed_submission_can_be_confirmed_on_a_later_attempt` (usage.rs:588) covers submitted versus sent across a failed attempt and a retry.
- `tool_outcomes_are_distinct_and_unknown_names_do_not_leak_model_text` (usage.rs:557) covers tool-call, failure and skipped counts, and that `inputs` stays empty when only `list_files` and `outline` are called.
- `throttled_requests_retry_unchanged_and_record_every_attempt` (mod.rs:637) shows `submitted_in_request` 0 and `sent_in_request` 8 after eight failed attempts.
- The CLI test `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` is an end-to-end run. It checks:
  - habeas, ripgrep and list_files calls;
  - 6 tool calls in total, with one habeas failure;
  - a repeated habeas read recorded as `unique == false`;
  - `sent_in_request`;
  - mandatory `definition` bytes greater than zero;
  - no source content in the usage log.
- tools.rs tests assert `list_files` yields no inputs.

**Interpretive choices**

- The "counts by evidence kind" are per-input records carrying `kind`, not pre-aggregated totals.
- "Sent" means a response with usage was received.

Both are reasonable readings of the text.
